A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MotionPRO research work, with 15 readable pages covering the main paper, references, and supplementary Sections 8–11. Text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose and trajectory experiments, ablations, humanoid simulation results, and a real-robot demonstration in Sections 5–6, Tables 2–6, and Figure 8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and simulation results, together with the supplementary dataset analyses.

M1.justification: The pressure-only network, LSAM, FRAPPE cross-attention fusion, training objectives, and robot pressure-refinement procedure are unchanged, including supplementary Sections 9–10.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MotionPRO's 70 participants, 400 motion types, and 12.4M frames; the same pressure-only and fused pose/trajectory tasks; and the same simulated and real-robot scenarios. Supplementary dataset-distribution comparisons also match.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout: IC and IC[FT] in Table 2; VIBE, CLIFF, SMPLer-X, TRACE, WHAM, and PhysPT in Table 3; TRACE and WHAM in Table 4; and Optical, CLIFF, and CLIFF-P in Table 6.

E3.justification: The participant-based 5:1 training/test split, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, 100-frame trajectory segments and alignment procedures, and NAO/Webots simulation setting are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 retains the same LSAM, FCAM, contact-loss, and 2D-loss ablations. The qualitative pose/trajectory cases and supplementary pressure and motion-distribution analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed evaluations, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 2–6 and the main and supplementary figures match. For example, FRAPPE's Table 3 MPJPE remains 41.8 mm and Table 4 RTE remains 41.6 mm; reported rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The contact-label definition in Equation 1, objectives in Equations 2–3, and supplementary loss definitions in Equations 4–8 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims for MotionPRO, FRAPPE, and pressure's benefits for pose estimation, global trajectories, and humanoid actuation.

C2.justification: The interpretations of pressure information, the 2D/3D loss tradeoff, and reduced robot completion despite more accurate poses are unchanged. Supplementary Sections 10–11 retain the same applicability qualifications and future directions.

D1.justification: Sensor and synchronization details, fixed body shapes, 20-frame inputs, frozen RGB encoder, AdamW learning rate of 5e-5, four RTX 4090D GPUs, and the stated project-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 65 numbered references retain the same cited works and research positioning. Novelty framing and relationships to earlier methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The acknowledgements change NSFC grant No.62171255 to No.62422110, and the arXiv stamp updates the version and date. Apart from whitespace differences in extraction, the research prose, headings, and section order are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–16 and Tables 1–6 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. Visual inspection and matching embedded images, vector drawings, and image placements confirm unchanged main-paper and supplementary layouts.

improvement.justification: The only content edit is a funding-identifier update, alongside the updated arXiv stamp. Methods, empirical support, interpretations, reproducibility information, and presentation remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
